title: CLAUDE.md
text: Everything mrmhub revolves around single S4 class MRMhubExperiment (R/classes.R). ’s container tibbles + processing state one experiment. Functions mostly pure-ish transforms shape mexp -> mexp — take MRMhubExperiment, return new one updated slots, flip status flags (is_istd_normalized, is_quantitated, is_filtered, is_isotope_corr, etc.). load-bearing convention — new processing functions must follow (first arg = MRMhubExperiment, return = MRMhubExperiment, update flags, never mutate dataset_orig). Functions returning bare tibble accepting raw columns break composability pipeline feel native API. Recommended pipeline order (enforced status flags, hard errors — see manual-10-design-decisions.Rmd): import_data_* → add_metadata → set_analysis_order → normalize_by_istd → correct_drift_* → correct_batch_* → quantify_by_istd / quantify_by_calibration → calc_qc_metrics → filter_features_qc → save_report_xlsx. Drift batch correction QC-sample-based (Broadhurst 2018) — never use study samples fitting. Importer family (manual-05a--importer.Rmd decision tree): import_data_mrmhub (preferred — INTEGRATOR’s long output), import_data_masshunter, import_data_skyline, import_data_csv_wide, import_data_csv_long, import_data_folder (multi-file batches). Feature variables carry _orig / _raw / _before / _beforecal / _fit postfix step overwrites . See manual-03-feature-variables.Rmd. Don’t invent new postfixes — extend existing set. Key slots (see R/classes.R full list R/mrmhub-global-definitions.R column templates): dataset_orig — long-format tibble raw imported data (one row per analysis × feature). Required cols: analysis_id, raw_data_filename, acquisition_time_stamp, feature_id. dataset — long-format working tibble metadata join + processing. Carries feature_intensity, feature_norm_intensity, feature_conc, qc_type, batch_id, etc. dataset_filtered — shape dataset, populated filter_features_qc(). annot_* — metadata tables (annot_analyses, annot_features, annot_istds, annot_responsecurves, annot_qcconcentrations, annot_studysamples, annot_batches). metrics_qc, metrics_calibration — derived QC/calibration metrics per feature. parameters_processing, status_processing — record run. var_drift_corrected, var_batch_corrected — per-variable booleans tracking feature_intensity / feature_norm_intensity / feature_conc corrected. S4 + tibbles: R/mrmhub-global-definitions.R setOldClass(c("tbl_df","tbl","data.frame")) tibbles can occupy "tbl_df" slots. Empty prototypes slot stored pkg.env$table_templates consulted class prototype import functions enforce schema. add column dataset/annot table, update matching template mrmhub-global-definitions.R downstream code silently drop mis-type .

title: Design Overview: How Data Flows Through MRMhub
text: MRMhub processes targeted mass spectrometry data two stages: Stage 1 — INTEGRATOR detects, picks, integrates chromatographic peaks mzML files, producing standardized long-format CSV peak areas per feature per sample. covers: Peak detection, picking, integration Batch-aware file organization Vendor raw files (.wiff, .d, .raw) first converted mzML separate tool (ProteoWizard MSConvert) INTEGRATOR run. Stage 2 — QUANT (R package) takes long CSV provides: Data import validation Internal standard (ISTD) normalization Drift batch correction External calibration quantification Quality control metrics filtering Visualization reporting

title: Design Overview: How Data Flows Through MRMhub
code: library(mrmhub)  # 1. Import data into MRMhubExperiment mexp <- MRMhubExperiment(analysis_type = "lipidomics") |>   import_data_csv_long(path = "path/to/long.csv")  # 2. Add metadata (sample and feature annotations) mexp <- add_metadata(mexp,                      metadata = list(annot_analyses = annot_analyses,                                      annot_features = annot_features))  # 3. Set analysis order (critical for drift correction) mexp <- set_analysis_order(mexp)  # 4. Normalize by internal standards mexp <- normalize_by_istd(mexp)  # 5. Correct drift (within-batch signal drift) mexp <- correct_drift_loess(mexp)  # 6. Correct batch effects (between-batch) mexp <- correct_batch_centering(mexp)  # 7. Quantify (using ISTD or external calibration) mexp <- quantify_by_istd(mexp) # -- OR -- mexp <- quantify_by_calibration(mexp)  # 8. QC filtering mexp <- calc_qc_metrics(mexp) mexp <- filter_features_qc(mexp)  # 9. Export save_report_xlsx(mexp, "results.xlsx")

what: Decision 1: S4 Class (MRMhubExperiment) vs Tidy Tibbles
title: Design Decisions: Why This Architecture?
text: Choice: single S4 object holds data, metadata, processing state. Rationale: Traceability — S4 object bundles original data, processed data, annotations, processing flags one place. Integrity checking — S4 validity methods ensure data metadata stay sync. Analyses accidentally deleted without updating annotations. Pipeline state — Flags like is_istd_normalized, var_drift_corrected prevent accidental double-processing. SummarizedExperiment — SE requires rectangular matrix layout (features × samples). Targeted MS data naturally long-format varying features per sample multiple intensity variables per measurement.
code: # The object structure: slotNames("MRMhubExperiment") #>  [1] "title"                "analysis_type"        "feature_intensity_var" #>  [4] "dataset_orig"         "dataset"              "dataset_filtered"      #>  [7] "annot_analyses"       "annot_features"       "annot_istds"           #> [10] "annot_responsecurves" "annot_qcconcentrations" "annot_studysamples" #> [13] "annot_batches"        "metrics_qc"           "metrics_calibration"   #> [16] "parameters_processing" "status_processing"   "is_istd_normalized"    #> [19] "is_quantitated"       "is_filtered"          "has_outliers_tech"     #> [22] "is_isotope_corr"      "analyses_excluded"    "features_excluded"     #> [25] "var_drift_corrected"  "var_batch_corrected"

text: Choice: feature_id represents unique compound (compound + adduct), transition. Rationale: MRM, compound may multiple transitions (quantifier + qualifiers). Peak integration (INTEGRATOR) selects best quantifier. time data reaches QUANT, feature one number per sample.

text: Choice: dataset_orig never modified import. processing operates dataset. Reproducibility: re-run step without re-importing Debugging: compare original vs processed verify corrections Auditability: raw data always accessible review

title: Design Decisions: Why This Architecture?
text: Choice: Drift batch correction exclusively based QC samples, never study samples. Reference: Broadhurst et al. (2018). Metabolomics, 14, 72. Implication: Sufficient QC samples (≥ 5 per batch, evenly distributed) required correction work well.

text: MRMhub set tools reproducible raw data processing, post-processing, quality control, reporting targeted quantitative small-molecule mass spectrometry experiments using Multiple Reaction Monitoring (MRM). platform includes two complementary tools: INTEGRATOR: standalone application automated peak detection, picking, integration mzML files. QUANT: R package providing function library data post- processing, including quantitation, data corrections, quality control, reporting. modular functionalities defined data structures support diverse analytical designs, data formats, processing tasks, found metabolomics, lipidomics quantitative small molecule analyses. Metadata has following warnings and notifications: #> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- #> # A tibble: 4 × 5 #>   Type  Table    Column                Issue                           Count #>   <chr> <chr>    <chr>                 <chr>                           <int> #> 1 W*    Analyses analysis_id           Analyses not in analysis data      15 #> 2 W*    Features feature_id            Feature(s) not in analysis data     4 #> 3 W*    Features feature_id            Feature(s) without metadata         1 #> 4 W*    ISTDs    quant_istd_feature_id Internal standard(s) not used       1 #>  #> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- #> E = Error, W = Warning, W* = Suppressed Warning, N = Note #> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- #> ✔ Analysis metadata associated with 499 analyses. #> ✔ Feature metadata associated with 502 features. #> ✔ Internal Standard metadata associated with 17 ISTDs. #> ✔ Response curve metadata associated with 12 annotated analyses. validated <- assert_metadata(   myexp,   metadata = list(annot_analyses = annot_analyses,                   annot_features = annot_features),   ignore_warnings = FALSE,   excl_unmatched_analyses = FALSE )  myexp <- add_metadata(myexp, metadata = validated)

title: Basic MRMhub Workflow
text: Apply normalization, quantification, drift correction, batch correction, QC filtering: Note drift correction uses study samples (ref_qc_types = "SPL") reference. Study-sample smoothing appropriate large, well-randomised sample sets; QC-based convention (Broadhurst et al. 2018) instead fits drift trend dedicated QC injections. recommended order : Normalize ISTD Quantify (ISTD external calibration) Drift correction Batch correction QC filtering See Design Overview full pipeline diagram.
code: # Normalize by internal standards myexp <- normalize_by_istd(myexp) #> ! Interfering features defined in metadata, but no correction was applied. Use `correct_interferences()` to correct. #> ✔ 460 features normalized with 17 ISTDs in 499 analyses.  # Quantify using ISTD-based approach myexp <- quantify_by_istd(myexp) #> ✔ 460 feature concentrations calculated based on 42 ISTDs and sample amounts of 499 analyses. #> ℹ Concentrations are given in μmol/L.  # Correct run-order drift (Gaussian kernel, sample-based) myexp <- correct_drift_gaussiankernel(   data = myexp,   variable = "conc",   ref_qc_types = c("SPL") ) #> ℹ Applying `conc` drift correction... #> ℹ 2 feature(s) contain one or more zero or negative `conc` values. Verify your data or use `log_transform_internal = FALSE`. #>  ■■■■■■■■■■■                       33% |  ETA:  5s #>  ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■            69% |  ETA:  3s #> ! 1 features showed no variation in the study sample's original values across analyses.  #> ! 1 features have invalid values after smoothing. NA will be be returned for all values of these faetures. Set `use_original_if_fail = FALSE to return orginal values.. #> ✔ Drift correction was applied to 459 of 460 features (batch-wise). #> ℹ The median CV change of all features in study samples was -0.56% (range: -10.22% to 2.49%). The median absolute CV of all features across batches decreased from 38.96% to 38.56%.  # Correct batch effects (median centering) myexp <- correct_batch_centering(   myexp,    variable = "conc",   ref_qc_types = "SPL" ) #> ℹ Adding batch correction on top of `conc` drift-correction. #> ✔ Batch median-centering of 6 batches was applied to drift-corrected concentrations of all 502 features. #> ℹ The median CV change of all features in study samples was -0.44% (range: -27.90% to 10.30%). what: 5. Univariate outlier detection on PC scores
title: QC Exploration with PCA
text: detect_outlier_pca() flags analyses whose score chosen principal component lies outside user-defined fence. fence defined either mean ± k·SD (outlier_detection = "sd") median ± k·MAD (outlier_detection = "mad"); fence_multiplicator sets k. function returns character vector analysis_id values exceed fence selected PC, NULL none flagged. Important: sample flagged PCA candidate investigation, verdict. Outlier patterns frequently reflect genuine biology (e.g. disease group, sex difference). exclude injection documented technical cause identified — failed injection, contamination, instrument fault, sample-handling error.
code: outlier_ids <- detect_outlier_pca(   mexp,   variable = "norm_intensity",   filter_data = FALSE,   pca_component = 1,   qc_types = c("BQC", "SPL"),   outlier_detection = "mad",   fence_multiplicator = 4 )  outlier_ids

title: QC Exploration with PCA

title: Interference Correction
text: Interference correction considered : blank injections show non-zero signal feature zero; two features biologically uncorrelated show strong injection--injection correlation suggestive cross-talk; theoretical M+1 / M+2 contribution adjacent species large enough bias measurement (typically percent target signal expected concentrations). Small contributions (~1% target signal) rarely justify correction; documented necessarily subtracted, since propagated uncertainty correction can exceed bias removed.

title: Interference Correction
text: correct_interferences() reads interference relationships defined annot_features. Two columns consulted: Features without interference assignment leave columns empty (NA). relationships chained (→ B → C, .e. C interferes B interferes ), set sequential_correction = TRUE (default) downstream features corrected first. affected feature correction subtracts interfering contribution: Valuecorrected=Valuetarget−fcontribution⋅Valueinterfering \text{Value}_\text{corrected} = \text{Value}_\text{target} -    f_\text{contribution} \cdot \text{Value}_\text{interfering} Negative results kept default; setting neg_to_na = TRUE replaces NA emits warning. Circular dependencies interference graph (→ B → ) detected aborted informative error. Add interference_feature_id interference_contribution annot_features table — table defines feature classes ISTD assignments. MRMhub Metadata Organizer template includes columns; plain save_metadata_templates() output well recent versions package.

title: Interference Correction
text: Contribution factors can derived three sources varying confidence: Theoretical natural-abundance isotopologue calculation — compute M+n fraction neutral formula using enviPat (Loos et al. 2015) comparable tools, scale instrument-specific transmission differences across two transitions. Empirical measurement — inject pure standard interfering species measure ratio signal target transition signal transition. captures instrument-specific effects (Q1/Q3 resolution, cross-talk, -source fragmentation) theoretical calculation omits. Published values — class-level interference tables published lipid panels shared precursor scans. Useful starting point verified empirically migrating methods instruments. reported M+2 fraction theoretical isotopologue abundance . real interference factor also depends Q1/Q3 transmission, -source fragmentation, chromatographic resolution two species. Validate blank pure-standard injections applying broadly.
code: library(enviPat) data(isotopes)  # PC 32:0 — neutral formula C40H80NO8P pattern <- isopattern(isotopes, "C40H80NO8P", charge = 1, threshold = 0.01)  # M+2 abundance relative to M+0 m_plus_2 <- pattern[[1]] m_plus_2[, "abundance"] / max(m_plus_2[, "abundance"])

title: Calculate Average Molecular Weight from Chemical Formulas — calc_average_molweight
text: function calculates average molecular weight (monoisotopic mass), reflects average isotopic distribution found nature. Isotopes can specified explicitly formula. Atomic mass numbers isotopes must enclosed square brackets (e.g., [13]C carbon-13). title: mrmhub 0.9.2
text: New save_dataset_mztab() writes processed MRMhubExperiment HUPO-PSI mzTab-M 2.0.0-M standard format (format expected repositories MetaboLights). analysis becomes assay, feature Small Molecule Feature (SMF) row grouped Small Molecule Summary (SML) rows analyte. abundance variable selectable via variable (default "conc", fall-back raw intensity unquantified data), metadata header can enriched instrument, contact publication. Output validator-passing official LIFS mzTab-M validator. New import_data_mztab() imports mzTab-M files produced tools (e.g. Lipid Data Analyzer, MS-DIAL, MZmine). SMF becomes feature assay analysis; per-assay abundances imported feature_intensity, feature identities study_variable grouping (batch_id) carried available. directions pure R add runtime dependency. See Import & Export mzTab-M recipe article.

what: Handling of analytical sequence gaps in plot_runscatter() and plot_rla_boxplot()
title: mrmhub 0.9.2

title: mrmhub 0.9.2
text: label_wrap label_wrap_width allow long feature_id strip labels wrapped across multiple lines. Set label_wrap = TRUE enable wrapping; use label_wrap_width control maximum line width characters (default: 25).

what: Plotting multiple response curves per feature in plot_responsecurves()
title: mrmhub 0.9.2
text: plot_responsecurves() gains following new arguments: curve_layout — one "overlay", "rows", "cols". "overlay" plots curves panel; "rows" splits curve separate row features columns; "cols" splits curve separate column features rows. Use fixed_scale_curves = TRUE fix y-axis upper limit maximum value across curves feature. r2_vstep — adjusts vertical spacing R² labels different curves curve_layout = "overlay".
